title: A priority queue: remove the largest
summary: Take the root, move the last value to the top, then swap it down below its larger child.

checkpoints.text: The root, 50, is the largest value: it is saved to be returned. The last value, 35, moves into the root, and `size` shrinks by one.
35 is compared with its children, 30 and 40. The larger child, 40, is bigger than 35, so it has to come up.
35 is now in cell 2, which has no children inside the heap, so it stops. 50 is returned, and the heap is valid again with 40 at the root.
Served first 50, then 40: a priority queue always hands out the most important item next, not the oldest. Removing costs O(log n) and finding the largest is O(1): it is always at the root.
